title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 20 (Place of arbitration)

content.overview: Section 20 allows the parties to agree on the place of arbitration. Failing agreement, the place is determined by the arbitral tribunal having regard to the circumstances of the case, including the convenience of the parties. The tribunal may meet at any place for consultation, hearings or inspection unless otherwise agreed.
content.glance: Agree the place; else tribunal decides; meetings may occur elsewhere for convenience unless agreed otherwise.
content.study: Party agreement on place controls. Failing agreement, the tribunal determines the place having regard to the circumstances, including convenience. Meetings for hearings or inspection may be held elsewhere unless the parties agree otherwise.

sections.heading: Party agreement
sections.body: Parties may agree on the place of arbitration.

sections.heading: Tribunal determination
sections.body: Failing agreement, the tribunal determines the place having regard to the circumstances, including convenience of the parties.

sections.heading: Meetings at other places
sections.body: Unless otherwise agreed, the tribunal may meet elsewhere for consultation, hearings, or inspection.
